Prerequisites include basic programming skills and familiarity with Python, as well as a basic understanding of linear algebra and calculus. The course will cover topics such as supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, and deep learning architectures, as well as the use of popular libraries and frameworks like TensorFlow and Keras. expanded_query: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamentals of public health and epidemiology, designed for individuals without a clinical background. Students will develop a solid understanding of the principles of epidemiology, including the measurement of disease frequency and risk, the study of disease distribution and determinants, and the application of epidemiologic methods in public health practice. Topics will include the epidemiologic triangle, disease surveillance, outbreak investigation, and the role of data analysis in informing public health policy and decision-making. By the end of the course, students will be able to apply epidemiologic concepts to real-world scenarios, identify and interpret relevant data, and communicate effectively with public health professionals. (Prerequisites: None; Target duration: 6-8 hours)

Prerequisites include a basic understanding of human development and behavior, as well as a willingness to engage with complex emotional and psychological concepts. Over the course of 12-16 hours, learners will develop skills in identifying and responding to mental health needs, understanding the impact of trauma and adversity, and applying evidence-based interventions to support individuals in crisis. Topics covered will include the biopsychosocial model, cognitive-behavioral theory, and the principles of person-centered care.
